t: The AI Hardware War, Antitrust, and the Future of Human Agency
s: This article explores Google's antitrust losses in the context of historical cases like AT&T and Microsoft, focusing on how the evolution of browser search bars ('omnibar') created a de facto monopoly over internet navigation and information access, with profound implications for AI development and human agency.
sub: Evolution of browser search bars (omnibar) from separate address and search fields to a single input, blurring the lines between navigation and search.
Google's antitrust losses in app store and search cases, and their potential remedies (choice screens, data sharing, ad-tech divestiture).
Historical antitrust cases (AT&T breakup, Microsoft/Netscape) as precedents for current tech giants.
The strategic importance of controlling the default search engine for user interaction and data flow on devices.
